pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/useWindowedRows.ts:153 The shared windowing hook gives each mounted row its position only as a data attribute, never as an ARIA position or set size, so assistive technology reads the mounted subset's size and offsets as the whole list's — the cost rung 4 of the performance technique says a windowed table must pay back.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/useWindowedRows.ts:153 Rows are keyed by identity (getItemKey -> keys[i]), but RowProps declares no aria-posinset/aria-setsize (or aria-rowindex/rowcount), so the full-set position is not re-declared under windowing.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/useWindowedRows.ts:120 One tab stop (roving tabindex); arrows clamp at the edges instead of wrapping; End goes to rows.length - 1 (the true end, since every row is held) and scrolls there before focusing; focus is keyed by row identity (line 71), not by index.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/query.ts:77 Read state keeps loading (pending), error, and last good data apart; data survives a failed refetch and is flagged stale instead of hidden, so error is never collapsed into empty.

apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/query.ts:34 Reads are keyed by their arguments (keys.ts keyOf), so an answer to a superseded predicate is never shown under the current one: latest-wins by key, including its error.
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/data/useWindowedRows.ts:1 The stated scale is hundreds to thousands of rows, orders of magnitude below the browser's scroll-size ceiling.

pairs.evidence: crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:249 The server-side Book query returns its rows with an honest truncation bound but does not echo the filter, group and range it answered, so the response's count is not structurally bound to its predicate, as the client-server-split contract requires (the client's argument-keyed cache makes up for this today, but the contract itself does not carry it).

techniques.evidence: crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:249 The allowlist is realized (fields and groups go through closed enums, book.rs:40, with values bound), but the response carries no echo of the query state it answered.
crates/table-ledger/src/audit.rs:233 audit_page is keyset pagination on the unique, immutable seq, and fetches limit + 1 rows (line 236) to report hasMore instead of an exact total.
crates/table-ledger/src/repositories.rs:599 Deal and audit reads order by the row identity (id / seq), which is a total, deterministic order.
crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:182 Rung 1: the Book query is always bounded (500 rows by default) and flags a cut answer as truncated, never sending the whole set.

pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/ListEngine.tsx:119 The list engine sorts with the caller's comparator alone and never adds the row identity it already holds (getKey) as a final tiebreaker, so rows with equal sort values fall in whatever order the input arrived in rather than a total, deterministic order.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/ListEngine.tsx:119 No identity tiebreaker. The comparators callers pass (e.g. 'largest' by amount alone, 'newest' with absent stamps coerced to 0) are not total either, and absent values change ends with direction.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/ListEngine.tsx:136 All-client regime, yet the text predicate is debounced (120 ms) instead of applied on each keystroke with the row derivation deferred, which the technique names as reintroducing the guess. Chips commit on change, the count is a role=status message (line 202), clear is one action, and the picked row is intersected with the shown rows at read time (line 147).

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/ListEngine.tsx:223 Windowed listitems are keyed by identity, and search text is built once per data change, but no aria-setsize/aria-posinset is declared, so a screen reader hears the mounted subset as the whole list.
